forces: Contract 1.1.0 lets a derived risk result declare derived_server while its only material input is a client_claim, and lets it omit derived_from entirely, so neither an over-claimed level nor an unlisted input is detectable.

The ratified derived-field-trust-semantics capability fixes maximum output trust as the lesser of the least trusted material input in the closure and the transformation ceiling, and classifies mandatory provenance with an enforced floor as a breaking major contract move.

Input trust must come from somewhere the producer cannot choose, or the producer supplies the number the floor compares against; the contract already declares a trust for every field and every extension namespace.
The risk model is the contract's only provenance carrier, so the transitive-closure rule is only complete if a self-referencing input is excluded rather than expanded.
1.1.0 admits derived_from only beside derived_server, which leaves a model whose floor is client_claim with no truthful representation once the floor is enforced.

Two validators implement the provenance outcomes from one generated block — the SDK semantic kernel and the contract fixture validator — and #423 showed they drift unless both move in the same change.

A contract version move touches more pins than regeneration reaches, and #95 left four behind in areas its owned paths already partly claimed; the inventory in CLAUDE.md is the list this move must advance.
SDK errors carry a code, category, and bounded path and never caller data, while the ratified rule says the floor diagnostic names the input that set it.

approach-floor-on-optional-provenance.reason: Omitting derived_from would still escape the floor, so the unlisted-input gap stays open, and the ratified capability classifies enforcement as a breaking major move: changing which 1.1.0 events are valid without changing the version misstates the contract.

approach-event-carried-input-trust.reason: The producer would supply the comparison value, so a producer could raise its own floor by raising the trust it reports for an input — the escalation the floor exists to prevent.

approach-schema-encoded-floor.reason: The floor needs the declared trust of each listed path, which the structural validator would have to embed per path; distinct semantic outcomes would collapse into one schema failure, and the collector's byte-identical vendored validator would gain semantic judgment it is specified not to hold.
